title: Projects
text:
ClimEx II
2022 – 2025
One of my largest projects to date. Using single-model large ensembles (SMILEs) to decompose climate model output into forced signal, bias and internal variability, with application to drought. Contributions include a multivariate bias correction method based on zero-inflated vine copulas (VBC), a generalised-additive-model framework for quantifying the spatio-temporal structure of internal variability, its application to a standardised drought index revealing a near-certain southeastern European drought hotspot under +3°C warming, and a deep-learning drought forecasting framework that propagates ensemble-derived uncertainty into probabilistic forecasts. See the publication on vine copula bias correction.

title: Henri Funk
text:
I’m a PhD candidate at the Chair of Statistics, LMU Munich, working in cooperation with the group of Physical Geography and Complex Environmental Systems, and a member of the Statistical Consulting Unit (StaBLab).
My research decomposes climate model uncertainty into bias and internal variability, with a focus on droughts: multivariate bias correction with vine copulas, uncertainty quantification, and algorithm-agnostic interpretability for clustering.
CV   Teaching   Publications   Projects   Contact

title: Henri Funk
text:
Research interests
My work centers on droughts and climate extremes: decomposing climate model uncertainty into bias, internal variability and forced signal, and carrying that decomposition through to drought characterisation and forecasting.
Statistical methods — I’m broad and pragmatic here, applying whatever suits the problem:

Uncertainty decomposition and quantification (aleatoric/epistemic)
Multivariate bias correction & copula modelling
Generalised additive models
Deep learning for probabilistic forecasting
Explainable / algorithm-agnostic machine learning

Geographic & domain focus — centered on climate models:

Droughts and compound climate extremes
Internal variability of single-model large ensembles (SMILEs)
European drought hotspots under future warming
Hydrology & meteorology, streamflow deficits
River water temperatures & riverine heatwaves
